title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with new contracts and strategic partnerships, while the specter of budget increases looms large. Meanwhile, the ongoing challenges in hypersonic testing remind us that not all advancements come easily.

themes.title: Contract Wins and Partnerships
themes.body: Viasat's $307 million contract with the Marine Corps highlights the ongoing demand for robust satellite communications. Additionally, Rocket Lab's plans to acquire a robotics company signal a push towards integrating more advanced technologies into launch operations.

themes.title: International Agreements on Space
themes.body: Paraguay's signing of the Artemis Accords indicates a growing global consensus on cooperative space exploration. This trend could reshape international partnerships and policy frameworks in the coming years.

themes.title: Budget Increases for Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's $1.4 billion boost for space resilience underscores a heightened focus on safeguarding national interests in orbit. This funding may pave the way for more innovative defense solutions and infrastructure.

themes.title: Hypersonic Testing Delays
themes.body: The continued delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle testing serve as a sobering reminder of the complexities involved in cutting-edge defense technologies. As the third quarter slips by without progress, stakeholders may need to reassess timelines and expectations.
